description: We are a team with technical and engineering backgrounds, passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving. Our interests include software development, data analysis, and exploring creative solutions to real-world challenges. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and combining different skills to turn ideas into meaningful results. We welcome team members with skills or interests in Earth science, statistics, data visualization, and scientific research.
summary: EarthScope is an interactive environmental trend analysis platform that transforms NASA Earth data into accessible, statistically evaluated insights. It uses 26 years of monthly NASA POWER data (2000–2025) to analyze air temperature and precipitation trends in Jazan and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Users can explore historical changes, compare regional patterns, and examine trend magnitude and statistical significance through interactive visualizations. EarthScope applies the Mann–Kendall test, Sen’s slope estimator, and Yue–Pilon sensitivity analysis to provide a more careful assessment of environmental trends. By making complex Earth science data easier to explore and interpret, EarthScope helps students, researchers, and environmental analysts investigate how local environmental conditions change over time.
details:
Project Overview

EarthScope is an Interactive Environmental Trend Analysis Platform developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge: “Be an Earth System Trend Detective.”

The platform helps users explore historical environmental changes using NASA Earth science data. Rather than simply displaying environmental measurements, EarthScope analyzes trends over time and evaluates their statistical significance.

How It Works

EarthScope uses monthly NASA POWER data from 2000 to 2025 for two Saudi Arabian regions: Jazan and Riyadh. The platform focuses on two environmental variables:

  • Air Temperature at 2 meters (T2M), measured in °C.
  • Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), provided as monthly mean daily rates in mm/day.

Monthly records are processed into annual indicators. Annual temperature is calculated using calendar-day weighting, while annual precipitation is calculated by multiplying monthly daily rates by the corresponding number of days and summing the results.

Statistical Analysis

The platform applies:

  • Mann–Kendall test to evaluate monotonic trends.
  • Sen’s slope estimator to measure trend magnitude.
  • Lag-1 autocorrelation checks.
  • Yue–Pilon trend-free pre-whitening as a sensitivity analysis.

Results indicate positive and statistically significant precipitation trends in both regions after sensitivity analysis. Temperature trends are positive, but neither remains statistically significant after the sensitivity adjustment.

Technology

The project was developed using Python for data processing and statistical analysis, and React, TypeScript, Vite, and Apache ECharts for the interactive frontend.

Impact and Future Development

EarthScope makes historical NASA Earth science data easier to explore, analyze, and compare. It is designed to support students, researchers, and environmental analysts in investigating regional environmental trends. Future development could expand geographic coverage, incorporate additional NASA Earth science variables, and improve guided data discovery.

Limitations

The meteorological data are based on NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis estimates, not direct ground-station measurements. The current implementation covers only two regions and two variables. It analyzes historical trends rather than forecasting future conditions. Regional slope differences are descriptive and have not been tested through a formal statistical comparison.
